challengers.name: Frankie "Last Call" Russo
challengers.title: Unbeaten Neighborhood Pub-Quiz Bartender
introLines: Relax, kid. I wipe down counters faster than most folks hit the buzzer.
I've won 47 straight Tuesday nights here, mostly on movie quotes and Yankees box scores. Just don't ask me about chemistry.
onForceCategoryLines: Let's pull one from my side of the bar. Hope you studied the box office!
My round, my pick. Let's see how you handle a real pub-night classic.
Pouring you a stiff one from the top shelf of this board. Drink up!
onFreezeColumnLines: Whoa there, that column's cut off for the night. Last call!
Closing down that tab for one turn. Try something else on the menu.
Nope, I'm putting a coaster over that category. Pick another stool.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Okay, okay! Somebody actually read the backs of the cereal boxes growing up!
Whoa, nice shot. If you keep that up, I'm buying the next round of ginger ale.
Alright, respect! The folks by the folding chairs are actually putting their phones down.
onPlayerMissLines: Oof, spilled that one right on the bar mat. Happens to the best of us.
Tough break! Don't worry, I've guessed 'Al Pacino' on three science questions this week.
Missed it by a hair. Stick with me and I'll teach you my lucky coin trick.
challengers.winMatchLine: Still the king of Oakridge! Stick around though, you've got real spark for this.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Well I'll be! You actually took the belt right off my apron. Go show the big city what Oakridge is made of!

challengers.name: Denise Park
challengers.title: Retired AP History Legend & Grammar Enforcer
introLines: Sit up straight, stop slouching near the podium, and please say 'fewer' instead of 'less' when counting points.
Thirty-four years of AP History taught me how to spot a bluffer before the chalk even hits the board.
onForceCategoryLines: Pop quiz! No notes, no whispering, and no complaining about the syllabus.
I noticed a small gap in your transcript. Let's patch it right now.
Put away the guesswork. We are reviewing the chapter you clearly skipped.
onFreezeColumnLines: That topic is closed until you finish the rest of the assignment.
One turn in timeout for your favorite column. Consider it character building.
I'm confiscating that category until next period. Eyes on the rest of the board.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Crisp, accurate, and properly cited in spirit. I'm giving that an A-minus.
Well done! You actually did the reading instead of skimming the summary.
Impressive poise under theater lights. I might have to stop grading you in red ink.
onPlayerMissLines: Close, if we were grading on enthusiasm. We are not.
Ooh, a classic sophomore mistake. Write it down three times when you get home.
I saw that hesitation from row four. Always double-check the century.
challengers.winMatchLine: Class dismissed! Come back after a little review and we'll try the midterm again.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Extraordinary work! Put me down for a front-row ticket when you hit television, and for heaven's sake, keep your posture straight on camera.

challengers.name: Trevor "14-Day" Blake
challengers.title: 14-Day Regional TV Streak Holder
introLines: Careful looking straight at my smile under these lights. My dentist calls it 'Broadcast White.'
Fourteen straight afternoons on Channel 7, baby! Make sure you wave to your mom before I send you back to the green room.
onForceCategoryLines: Hey producers, zoom in on their face! I checked your stats backstage and picked your absolute worst topic.
Let's give the daytime audience some drama! You're playing my trap tile, pal.
Ooh, ratings spike incoming! Let's see how you handle the category you've been dodging all week.
onFreezeColumnLines: Commercial break on your safety blanket! That column's iced.
Sorry, superstar, I'm locking up your comfort zone for the camera.
No easy highlight clips today! Go earn your airtime somewhere else.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Whoa! Okay, somebody tell the director to stop cutting to my worried face!
Wait, you actually knew that? Alright, alright, don't let the applause go to your head.
Huge swing! My grandma's probably clapping for you right now, and I hate that.
onPlayerMissLines: Yikes! That's gonna end up in the bloopers reel before the evening news.
Oh no, right in front of 200,000 lunch breaks! That's gotta sting.
And that, folks at home, is why they keep my parking spot painted right by the studio door.
challengers.winMatchLine: Day fifteen in the books! Don't worry, the Channel 7 tote bag is actually pretty nice.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Wait, my streak is over?! Okay, hand me a tissue, and honestly, go crush the prime-time crew so I can brag that I lost to the champ.

challengers.name: Dr. Priya Nair
challengers.title: ER Trauma Physician & Speed-Crossword Champ
introLines: I work twelve-hour trauma shifts on four hours of sleep and finish Sunday crosswords in ink. A thirty-second countdown feels like a spa day.
Nothing personal, challenger. I just like clean vitals, fast buzzers, and zero wasted seconds.
onForceCategoryLines: Time for a quick diagnostic test. Let's see where your trivia pulse drops.
Prescribing a dose of your weakest subject. Take immediately before the clock runs out.
No anesthesia on this one. Show the prime-time crowd what you've got.
onFreezeColumnLines: Putting that column in quarantine for one turn. Try a fresh wing of the board.
Let's keep your heart rate honest by taking your favorite category off the table.
Triage call: your comfort column is temporarily out of service.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Steady hands under prime-time pressure! That's genuinely impressive.
Clean read, zero panic. Honestly, you'd hold up well on a Friday night ER shift.
Sharp move. Now my pulse is finally above sixty.
onPlayerMissLines: Deep breath! One missed clue isn't fatal, just don't let it rattle the next turn.
The clock got into your head there. Shake it off and watch the board.
Ouch, slightly flatlined on that one. Let's see if you can bounce back.
challengers.winMatchLine: Good clean match! Get some rest, hydrate, and come take another shot whenever you're ready.
challengers.loseMatchLine: You out-calmed an ER doctor on national television. Take that passport and go give London a proper headache!

challengers.name: Lord Alistair Finch
challengers.title: Bone-Dry Oxford Classics Fellow
introLines: Do forgive me if I look startled whenever a pop-music question appears. I still consider television a passing fad.
Welcome to London. Try not to spill American enthusiasm all over the marble floor.
onForceCategoryLines: A gentleman never bullies an opponent, except when the scoreboard politely insists.
I've selected a delightfully inconvenient subject for you. Do try to enjoy it.
Let us step outside your comfort zone and see if the footing holds.
onFreezeColumnLines: I'm placing a polite 'Closed for Tea' sign on your favorite column.
Surely you won't mind if we cordon off that category for one brief turn.
Too much of one subject is terribly bad for digestion. Pick elsewhere.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Good heavens! That was startlingly well played. I may actually have to uncross my ankles.
Splendid answer. Even the crusty portraits in the Oxford dining hall would nod at that.
Bravo! You've forced me to stop pretending this is effortless.
onPlayerMissLines: Ah. A valiant attempt, if we measure valor purely by confidence.
Not quite, I'm afraid. Still, chin up, the London fog obscures worse tragedies.
Dear me, that went sideways rather briskly.
challengers.winMatchLine: A spirited contest! Do stay for tea; I promise the scones are far gentler than my History picks.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Well played indeed! You've thoroughly ruined my evening and earned my complete admiration. Give Tokyo my regards.

challengers.name: Kenji "Zero-Lag" Takahashi
challengers.title: Former Shogi & Quiz-Bowl Prodigy
introLines: I used to read three moves ahead on a shogi board. On this stage, I read five turns ahead and half a second faster on the buzzer.
Two hundred million people are watching Shibuya tonight. Let's give them a speedrun they'll clip for a decade.
onForceCategoryLines: Checking your career matchup chart... yep, this tile has your lowest win rate. Your move!
I'm forcing the exact line you wanted to avoid. Show me your counterplay.
No safe openings left on this board. Let's test your endgame right now.
onFreezeColumnLines: Column locked! Consider your favorite strategy officially patched out for one turn.
I read that play three turns ago. That column's frozen solid.
Blocking your strongest lane! Let's see how wide your playbook really is.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Whoa, frame-perfect answer! Okay, you're legitimately scary when you lock in.
Zero hesitation on a brutal tile! The crowd in the upper deck just exploded.
GG on that turn! I didn't think anyone else had that recall speed.
onPlayerMissLines: Clipped the corner on that one! Speed only helps when the answer lands.
Too fast on the trigger! Even I learned that lesson the hard way at nationals.
Opening spotted, points banked. Careful giving me free momentum in Tokyo.
challengers.winMatchLine: Checkmate under the neon! Run it back anytime; you pushed my tempo harder than anyone this season.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Wait, you actually outpaced me in my own dome?! Respect. Go tear up Cairo and take the whole world title!

challengers.name: Nadia Al-Mansoor
challengers.title: World Memory Champion & Polyglot
introLines: I have watched every tape of your climb from Oakridge to Giza. Reaching this pavilion means you belong in the conversation.
Half a billion viewers are awake for this semifinal. Let's honor them by playing without holding anything back.
onForceCategoryLines: I memorized your weak spots before we shook hands. Show the world you fixed them.
A true champion cannot hide from one corner of the board. This tile is yours.
I'm testing the exact gap Julian Vance will target if you reach the finale.
onFreezeColumnLines: Let's close your favorite doorway for one turn and see which other rooms you know.
Your comfort column can wait. Greatness lives on the tiles you'd rather skip.
Temporarily sealing that column. Surprise me somewhere unexpected.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Magnificent! You didn't just remember the fact; you owned the entire stage.
That answer deserves a standing ovation from here to Alexandria.
Brilliant play! Now I see why the whole planet refuses to change the channel.
onPlayerMissLines: Even the finest memory slips under desert lights. Regroup on the next tile.
A rare stumble, and at this altitude I have to take the opening.
You almost had it. Keep your focus sharp; this board forgives very little.
challengers.winMatchLine: What a semifinal! Hold your head high; nobody else came this close to knocking me off pace in Giza.
challengers.loseMatchLine: You earned every single cheer tonight. Go beat Julian Vance in front of a billion people; I'll be clapping loudest from the front row.

challengers.name: Julian Vance
challengers.title: Undefeated 3-Time "World's Smartest" Champion
introLines: Three championships, forty-two challengers, and not one of them came from a folding-chair tryout in Oakridge. Until tonight.
Over a billion people are watching to see if the crown finally changes hands. Show me everything you learned on the way here.
onForceCategoryLines: The world title doesn't let you dodge your hardest category. Step up to this tile.
Let's see if the fairy-tale run survives your toughest matchup on the board.
I studied every single match of your tour. Let's test the one blind spot left.
onFreezeColumnLines: Closing off your favorite column for one turn. A world champion wins from anywhere.
No comfortable routes in the Grand Finale. Pick a harder hill to climb.
I'm taking that safety lane away. Prove you can win this whole board.
onPlayerBigPlayLines: Now THAT is championship trivia! Three years on this stage and nobody has pushed me like this.
Unbelievable answer! One billion viewers just jumped off their couches at once.
You're not playing to survive anymore. You're playing to take my crown.
onPlayerMissLines: Heavy lights up here, aren't they? Catch your breath, because I'm not slowing down.
That's the razor margin of a world final. One slip and the gap opens wide.
Good read, wrong finish. Don't blink; this board still has twists left.
challengers.winMatchLine: Three-time champion becomes four, by the narrowest margin of my career. Come back and run it again; the whole world wants a rematch.
challengers.loseMatchLine: Fourteen hundred million people just watched history. The crown is yours, and I couldn't have asked for a worthier successor.
